title: Synthesis of Gold Nanoparticle Integrated Photo-responsive Liposomes and Measurement of Their Microbubble Cavitation upon Pulse Laser Excitation
protocol: Clean 100 ml round bottom flasks using aqua regia.
Wash the flasks with DI water.
Autoclave the flasks.
Dry the flasks in a hot air oven at 100 °C for 15 min.
Sterilize the hand-held mini-extruder set using 70% ethanol.
Turn on the rotary evaporator.
Set the temperature of the hot water bath to 37 °C.
Set the cooling tower temperature to 4 °C.
Prepare a 60 mM calcein stock solution by dissolving 374 mg of calcein in 10 ml of 0.1 mM PBS (pH 7.4).
Adjust the pH to 7.4 using 1 M sodium hydroxide (NaOH) solution.
Remove lipids from freezer and thaw them to room temperature.
Weigh 15.9 mg DPPC, 1.3 mg MPPC, and 2.8 mg DSPE-PEG2000.
Dissolve the lipids together in 2 ml chloroform.
Transfer the chloroform solution to a sterile round bottom flask.
Evaporate the solvent using the rotary evaporator under reduced pressure.
Hydrate the lipid layer at 45 °C with 2 ml aqueous solution containing 1.95 ml of 60 mM calcein and 50 µl Au NPs (3.36 × 10^16 particles/ml) for 30 min.
Pre-heat the heating block to 45 °C.
Place a 200 nm polycarbonate membrane filter between the filter supports and assemble the mini-extruder set.
Check the potential leakage with DI water.
Fill one syringe with 1 ml of liposome solution from step 2.4.
Extrude the sample by passing the solution to the other syringe end of the assembled mini-extruder.
Repeat extrusion 11 times.
Run the synthesized liposomes through a PD-10 desalting column to remove free Au NPs, lipids and calcein using PBS as eluent according to manufacturer's protocol.
Store the samples in sterile tubes at 4 °C for use within 2 days.
Calculate the lipid molarity of the stock solution by adding up the molarities of DPPC, MPPC, and DSPE-PEG2000 from step 2.2.
Dilute the liposome stock solution to a concentration of 5 mM using 0.1 mM PBS buffer (pH 7.4).
Transfer samples to a centrifuge tube (2 ml).
Place the tube in a hot water bath and raise temperature gradually from 25 to 70 °C at a rate of 1 °C/min.
Collect aliquots of 10 µl at different temperatures: 27, 32, 37, 39, 41, 43, 45, 52, 57, 62, 67 and 70 °C.
Add 10 µl of 2% Triton X-100 to a 2 ml aliquot of liposomal solution for complete calcein release after digesting at RT for 10 min.
Transfer 200 μl of the liposomal solution to each well in the 96-well microplate.
Measure the fluorescence intensity of the collected samples using a fluorescence microplate reader.
Use excitation and emission wavelengths of 480 nm and 515 nm, respectively, for calcein.
Take the fluorescence intensity of the Triton X-100 treated samples as 100% release.
Calculate the percentage of released calcein at each time point using the provided formula.
Transfer 100 μl liposome solution to a quartz cuvette.
Place the quartz cuvette in a cuvette holder.
Use a pulsed Nd:YAG laser with pulse duration of 6 nsec and wavelength of 532 nm as the light source.
Set the repetition rate to 1 Hz, laser energy density to 1 mJ/cm², and beam diameter to 0.5 mm.
Guide the collimated laser beam through the cuvette so that it passes through the liposome solution.
Collect aliquots after various pulses.
Add 10 μl of 2% Triton X-100 to 2 ml aliquot of liposomal solution for digestion at room temperature.
Digest the liposomes for 10 min to achieve complete release of calcein.
Pre-measure the bleaching effect of pulsed laser on calcein solution.
Expose calcein solution (60 mM) to pulsed laser with a frequency of 1 Hz for varying pulse numbers (0, 25, 50, and 100).
Measure the fluorescence intensity of calcein before and after laser exposure using excitation and emission wavelengths of 480 nm and 515 nm respectively.
Calculate the amount of bleaching as fluorescence intensity of calcein before laser exposure divided by the fluorescence intensity after specific pulse numbers.
Normalize values obtained from liposome samples by multiplying their fluorescence intensity with the calculated bleaching factor.
Measure the fluorescence intensity of collected samples using a fluorescence microplate reader at excitation and emission wavelengths of 480 nm and 515 nm respectively.
Take the fluorescence intensity of Triton X-100 treated samples as 100% release.

Calculate the percentage of released calcein at each pulse number using the formula: Ft is the normalized fluorescence intensity of solution at a given pulse number. Fi and Fx are the initial and final normalized fluorescence intensities respectively.
Place 100 µl of the sample on a microscopic slide.
Set the focus of the laser onto the sample.
Immerse a needle hydrophone (1 mm diameter and 450 nV/Pa sensitivity) into the solution.
Irradiate the sample with the pulsed laser with varying pulse numbers (0-100) and pulse energy (20-160 µJ/pulse).
Record the pressure signals using a digital oscilloscope.
